def warm_curriculum_caches():
    """Build the payload keys a Curriculum page load reads, for both visibilities.

    Deliberately the compact keys only. They are what the page actually asks for
    -- overview, modules, programmes -- and they share one rows read, so warming
    both visibilities costs a single trip to the database.

    The whole warm runs inside one read scope. On the request path each build
    opens its own, which is right there -- a request must not read back rows
    memoised before someone else's write. Here there is no such caller: this is
    one batch, assembling one consistent snapshot, and the two visibilities plus
    the enrichments otherwise re-read the same authoring tables several times
    over. curriculum.components alone is ~18k rows on a remote database and
    dominates the build, so reading it once is most of what warming saves.
    """
    from config.management_safety import reconciliation_command
    if reconciliation_command():
        return
    with curriculum_read_scope():
        for visibility in ('operational', 'all'):
            payload = cached_curriculum_value(
                f'overview:{visibility}:compact',
                lambda visibility=visibility: build_curriculum_payload(visibility, compact=True),
            )
            enriched_modules = cached_curriculum_value(
                f'modules:{visibility}:enriched',
                lambda visibility=visibility: enrich_modules_with_authoring(
                    payload['modules'], include_programme_deleted=visibility == 'all',
                ),
            )
            cached_curriculum_value(
                f'programmes:{visibility}:with-module-counts',
                lambda visibility=visibility: enrich_programmes_with_module_counts(
                    payload['programmes'], enriched_modules,
                    modules_enriched=True, include_archived=visibility == 'all',
                ),
            )
def _curriculum_warm_loop():
    from config.management_safety import reconciliation_command
    if reconciliation_command():
        return
    global _CURRICULUM_WARM_RUNNING, _CURRICULUM_WARM_REQUESTED
    try:
        while True:
            time.sleep(CURRICULUM_WARM_DELAY_SECONDS)
            with _CURRICULUM_WARM_LOCK:
                _CURRICULUM_WARM_REQUESTED = False
            started = datetime.now().timestamp()
            try:
                warm_curriculum_caches()
                logger.info(
                    'Curriculum cache warm finished in %.1fs.',
                    datetime.now().timestamp() - started,
                )
            except Exception:
                # A warm that fails must never take the process with it; the
                # request path still rebuilds on demand.
                logger.warning('Curriculum cache warm failed.', exc_info=True)
            try:
                # Apart from the warm above: that one is a single untargeted
                # read scope, and a programme build needs its own targeted one.
                warm_programme_detail_sections()
            except Exception:
                logger.warning('Programme section warm failed.', exc_info=True)
            finally:
                # This thread opened its own connection. Neon counts it, and a
                # warm runs rarely enough that holding one between runs is pure
                # cost.
                connections.close_all()
            with _CURRICULUM_WARM_LOCK:
                if not _CURRICULUM_WARM_REQUESTED:
                    _CURRICULUM_WARM_RUNNING = False
                    return

        with _CURRICULUM_WARM_LOCK:
            _CURRICULUM_WARM_RUNNING = False
        raise

    disabled case from the queued one.

    if reconciliation_command() or not CURRICULUM_WARM_ENABLED:
        return False

    with _CURRICULUM_WARM_LOCK:

            name='curriculum-cache-warm',

            _CURRICULUM_WARM_RUNNING = False

def stored_module_cover_image(module_catalogue_id, value):

    in a column every module list selects. Five modules doing it was 1.52 MB of a
    1.79 MB ``/curriculum/modules/?compact=true`` response, 83% of it, and the
    column is also read whole by the payload build and by My Learning. The
    picture is the same size either way; what changes is that a list of 281
    modules stops carrying it.

    So the bytes go where every other authoring upload goes -- Azure when it is
    configured, local disk when it is not -- and the column keeps the same
    ``/curriculum_api/curriculum/uploads/...`` URL shape a component upload
    stores. One cover per module, so the path has a fixed slot and a new upload
    simply replaces the old one.

    Anything that is not an inline value is returned untouched: an https:// URL
    a curator pasted is already a URL, and '' still means "remove the cover".

    A ``data:`` value is never handed back for a column. One that is not a
    base64 image of a known type, does not decode, or cannot be stored raises
    ``CoverImageError`` and the save is refused: no image is kept as base64.
    """
    value = clean_str(value)
    if not value.lower().startswith('data:'):
        return value
    match = MODULE_COVER_DATA_URI.match(value)
    content_type = match.group(1).lower() if match else ''
    if content_type not in MODULE_COVER_EXTENSIONS:
        raise CoverImageError('Choose a JPG, PNG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, SVG or BMP image.')
    try:
        raw = base64.b64decode(re.sub(r'\s+', '', match.group(2)), validate=True)
    except Exception:
        logger.warning('Module %s sent a cover image that is not valid base64.', module_catalogue_id)
        raise CoverImageError('The image could not be read. Choose it again.')
    if not raw:
        return ''
    module_segment = safe_upload_segment(module_catalogue_id, 'module')
    extension = MODULE_COVER_EXTENSIONS[content_type]
    timestamp = datetime.utcnow().strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S%f')
    relative_path = (
        f'{COMPONENT_UPLOAD_ROOT}/{module_segment}/{MODULE_COVER_UPLOAD_SLOT}/cover-{timestamp}{extension}'
    )
    try:
        saved_path = upload_storage.store(ContentFile(raw), relative_path, content_type)
    except Exception:
        logger.exception('Unable to store the cover image for module %s.', module_catalogue_id)
        raise CoverImageError('The image could not be uploaded right now. Try again.')
    public_path = saved_path.removeprefix(f'{COMPONENT_UPLOAD_ROOT}/')
    return f'/curriculum_api/curriculum/uploads/{public_path}'

    """Raised inside a save so the transaction rolls back before the 409.

    from inside ``transaction.atomic()`` would commit whatever the earlier
    iterations had already written, leaving half the save applied and the
    schedule in exactly the inconsistent state this check exists to prevent.

    def __init__(self, candidate, conflicts):
        super().__init__(tutor_conflict_message(candidate, conflicts))

def warm_programme_detail_sections():
    """Rebuild the recently read modules sections a write has made stale.

    Through cached_curriculum_value as a reader would, so a section the write
    did not touch costs one generation check, and a build that a later write
    overtakes is discarded rather than published.
    """
    now = time.monotonic()
    with _PROGRAMME_SECTION_WARM_LOCK:
        for target, seen in list(_PROGRAMME_SECTION_WARM_TARGETS.items()):
            if now - seen > PROGRAMME_SECTION_WARM_WINDOW_SECONDS:
                del _PROGRAMME_SECTION_WARM_TARGETS[target]
        targets = list(reversed(_PROGRAMME_SECTION_WARM_TARGETS))
    for identifier, visibility, workspace_view in targets:
        try:

        except Exception:
            logger.warning('Programme modules warm failed.', exc_info=True)

class StaleModuleStructureWrite(Exception):
    """An attachment tried to replace an existing module's weeks from an old copy."""

    def __init__(self, module_catalogue_id, expected_revision, current_revision):
        super().__init__(module_catalogue_id)
        self.module_catalogue_id = module_catalogue_id
        self.expected_revision = expected_revision
        self.current_revision = current_revision

    def as_response(self):
        if not self.expected_revision:
            return json_error(
                'This save would replace the weeks of a module that already exists, but it does not say '
                'which saved version of that module it was made from, so nothing was saved. Edit the '
                "module's weeks in the Module Builder.",
                status=428,
                conflict=True,
                moduleCatalogueId=self.module_catalogue_id,
            )
        return record_conflict_response(
            self.expected_revision, self.current_revision, moduleCatalogueId=self.module_catalogue_id,
        )
